children: The dollar has given up about half of its gains against the yen from the low marked in September, and the Y157 area may now serve as initial resistance, Marc Chandler of Bannockburn Capital Markets says in a note. The dollar declined last week against the yen likely due to a sharp drop in U.S. interest rates spurred by the intensification of the retreat from the artificial-intelligence trade, the chief market strategist says. Over the past 30 sessions, changes in the dollar-yen exchange rate have been the most correlated with changes in the two-year interest rate differential between U.S. and Japan government bond yields than the other financial variables that the firm tracks, he says. The dollar is at Y156.72. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)
